analysis: The two supplied units are BASE-side excerpts of desktop-app/package-lock.json (lines 2449-3957). They contain only unchanged lockfile entries (the @typescript/* platform binaries, app-builder-lib, electron-builder, electron 44.5.1 at ~3660, and others). The changed-range map shows the real changes are elsewhere or on the head side: electron 44.5.1 -> 44.9.1, vite 8.3.2 -> 8.3.5, @oxc-project/types 0.152 -> 0.155, @rolldown/binding-* 1.2.12 -> 1.2.15, plus related integrity hashes and a few additions around lines 5980-6010. Base line 3661 (electron version) falls in a changed range, but the new version and integrity values are visible only in the patch excerpt, which is truncated. I verified that the base entries in my units carry registry.npmjs.org resolved URLs with sha512 integrity fields and have no unusual git or tarball sources. Dependency bumps of this kind affect the desktop app build and runtime supply chain, not the provider boundaries in the threat model: TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011 and TB-012 are not touched. The App Attest, attestation and authorization controls (T-013, T-034, TB-011) are unaffected by this lockfile content. I did not see the head-side lockfile lines, so I could not check the new resolved URLs or integrity hashes. The truncated patch shows only registry.npmjs.org URLs. No security regression can be established from the supplied evidence. The remaining integration question is whether the head-side lockfile has any non-registry resolved sources or removed integrity fields in the unseen hunks at about 5980-6030, and whether the Electron bump stays aligned with the signed-app packaging config. I do not consider either an observed issue.
